answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a time-locked bond before it may submit jobs or vote on reputation updates. A kernel of validators slashes that bond when an agent is proven to double-spend or collude, while honest identities recover it after a cooling period. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must lock capital for each identity and risks losing it, rather than minting names for free. The bond can be ferrous in its rigidity, but a jetty of appeal checks helps prevent mistaken slashing.
